title: Pain, but not hypermobility, is associated with borderline personality disorder symptoms among individuals diagnosed with EDS or G-HSD.
abstract: Research examining borderline personality disorder (BPD) in individuals with Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes (EDS) and Generalized Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder (G-HSD) is limited, despite overlap between core BPD features (e.g., emotion dysregulation) and common EDS/G-HSD conditions (e.g., chronic pain). This study examined associations between BPD symptoms and EDS/G-HSD features. Data were from a retrospective chart review of patients evaluated at the GoodHope EDS Clinic between 2019-2021. Patients diagnosed with EDS or G-HSD (N=205) completed self-report measures of BPD symptoms and EDS/G-HSD features (i.e., pain severity/interference, autonomic symptom burden). Clinicians assessed joint hypermobility. An ANOVA examined group differences between individuals scoring above the recommended BSL-23 threshold (i.e., ≥ 1.5) and below the cut-off. A linear regression examined associations between EDS/G-HSD features and BPD symptom severity. Forty-five participants (22%) scored above the recommended BSL-23 threshold, indicating elevated BPD symptoms. These individuals reported greater pain severity, pain interference, and autonomic symptom burden compared to those below the cut-off score. In a linear regression, pain interference was the only EDS/G-HSD feature associated with BPD symptom severity; pain severity, joint hypermobility, and autonomic symptom burden were not significant. Greater pain interference was associated with more severe BPD symptoms among individuals with EDS/G-HSD. Further research is needed to clarify these relationships, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and improve interventions for this population.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY IN MEDICAL SETTINGS
